subject: Use when designing or maintaining the shape of a repository's git history — choosing a branching model, deciding…

evals.prompt: Define version-control in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the version-control skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind version-control. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "draft a Conventional Commits message for this change". Should version-control activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force version-control onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to code-review, refactor, naming-conventions, debugging, guardrails.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "set up trunk-based development for a four-person team". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying version-control.
Place version-control among its adjacent skills (code-review, refactor, naming-conventions, debugging, guardrails). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about version-control and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
